answer: No — that comparison doesn't support the switch. The Elastic Net WAPE and the Prophet WAPE come from two different, non-comparable setups: Prophet was scored on daily unit forecasts while Elastic Net was scored on monthly aggregates. Monthly aggregation smooths out day-to-day noise, which mechanically shrinks WAPE regardless of which model is actually better. For example, in FOODS_3 Prophet's daily WAPE is 19.81% vs Elastic Net's monthly WAPE of 4.86%, and in HOUSEHOLD_1 it's 21.56% vs 3.26% — the gap looks large but reflects the aggregation difference, not a 4x accuracy improvement at the planning (daily) level the backtest actually operates at. The tool data itself flags this: 'daily and monthly WAPE are not directly comparable.' Also note this Prophet/Elastic Net study is a separate benchmark from the planning-level forecast-vs-naive metrics used elsewhere in this backtest (where overall forecast accuracy is 79.5% vs a 85.2% naive baseline, i.e. the current model actually underperforms naive by 5.7pp on average). To make a real switch decision you'd need Elastic Net evaluated on the same daily basis, for all departments, which isn't available here.
